clue.text: Brown bread for health

definitions.meaning: a drink raised to wish someone good health

explanation.definitionFit: Grilled slices of bread and a raised-glass salute share one word, the second a tribute drunk to someone's wellbeing.

clue.text: Try to land

definitions.meaning: a score in rugby or American football
the moment an aircraft meets the ground

explanation.definitionFit: A rugby score grounding the ball and an aircraft's arrival on the runway share the name.

clue.text: Free transfer for Croat player

indicators.note: the letters move freely to new places, as a footballer moves clubs

explanation.surface: A Croatian footballer joins a club without a fee.
explanation.definitionFit: A player is a performer on stage.

clue.text: Pattern you would have to consider after study

indicators.note: what is left after study is taken from the front of the longer word

parts.note: to contemplate is to consider
to con is to study

explanation.surface: A design one must think over after some learning.
explanation.walkthrough: A subtraction clue: 'after' tells you to take the part of 'consider' that comes after the word for study.
explanation.definitionFit: A template is a pattern or guide for shaping copies.

clue.text: Story a child slept through?

parts.note: a kid is a child
napped means dozed, slept for a while

explanation.surface: A tale so dull a youngster dozed off during it.
explanation.walkthrough: The story is Robert Louis Stevenson's adventure novel of 1886.
explanation.definitionFit: Stevenson's novel about David Balfour is a famous adventure story.

clue.text: The bird is flown

definitions.meaning: a bird of prey of the hawk family
a toy flown on a string in the wind

explanation.definitionFit: A forked-tailed raptor and a paper toy on a string share the name.

clue.text: She's pretty stupid

parts.note: 'pretty stupid' reads as 'rather dim' but means good-looking and brainless, the stereotype of a fair-haired woman

explanation.definitionFit: The stock figure of an attractive but empty-headed fair-haired woman.

clue.text: Double bill — one with a Tree

indicators.note: doubled means the bill appears twice over

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Two invoices, one of them for a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The acacia is a thorny tree, the wattle of Australia.

clue.text: Start of parrot's brisk chatter

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: rattling means brisk, lively, as in a rattling pace

explanation.surface: The first squawks of a parrot's lively babbling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chatter' is a verb's gerund sense here: babbling talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Childish idle talk or babble is the sense shared with the verb-noun.

clue.text: Charles has his head in the sand, stupid boy

indicators.note: in means the letter goes inside the sandhill word

parts.note: a dune is a hill of sand

indicators.note: only the head, the first letter, of the name Charles is used

explanation.surface: Charles buries his head like an ostrich, the silly lad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head in the sand' is an idiom for ignoring trouble; here 'head' is C and 'in' places it inside DUNE.
explanation.definitionFit: A dunce is a slow pupil, the boy made to wear the conical cap.

clue.text: Final demand from Thule Corporation

parts.note: Thule is the far northern land of legend, called Ultima Thule, so the word brings in its companion ULTIMA
corporation is an old jokey word for a paunch, a tum

explanation.surface: A last warning letter from a company named Thule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' looks like a business; in crosswords it is a pot belly. Thule is clued by the Latin phrase Ultima Thule, the edge of the known world.
explanation.definitionFit: An ultimatum is a last set of terms whose rejection ends negotiations.

clue.text: A chief is flat out

parts.note: main means principal, chief

explanation.surface: A boss is exhausted or lying down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat out' seems to mean lying down or exhausted; here it means at full speed, an old sense of the adverb.
explanation.definitionFit: Amain is an archaic adverb meaning with full force or at top speed.

clue.text: Usher in York is one

definitions.meaning: to announce or bring in something new
York is the title of one of the officers of arms at the College of Arms

explanation.definitionFit: To announce a coming thing is to proclaim it, and York is a heraldic officer's title in England's College of Arms.

clue.text: Sailors in the Scrubs?

parts.note: ABs are able seamen, sailors
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Seamen locked up in Wormwood Scrubs prison.
explanation.walkthrough: Wormwood Scrubs is a London prison; the drink is distilled from wormwood, so 'Scrubs?' defines it by leaving out 'Wormwood'.
explanation.definitionFit: The green spirit is flavoured with wormwood, the plant whose name precedes Scrubs in the jail's name.

clue.text: Firm flesh near the knuckle?

parts.note: strong means firm, solid
meat is animal flesh

explanation.surface: Solid flesh close to the joint of a cut of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'near the knuckle' is a British idiom for close to indecent or offensive.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard-hitting material that shocks the squeamish is near the knuckle, risqué.

clue.text: Remote post, not in Victoria for example

parts.note: out is the opposite of in
Victoria is a London railway station

explanation.surface: A distant job, not in Victoria for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: Victoria is one of London's main railway stations.
explanation.definitionFit: An outstation is a branch or base far from headquarters.

clue.text: The sort of sketch that needs cutting

definitions.meaning: a brief, small outline drawing or description
the horny plate on the hand's shortest, thickest digit, which grows and must be trimmed

explanation.definitionFit: A quick miniature outline sketch is called after the plate on the stubbiest digit, which grows and is trimmed with clippers.

clue.text: Jude is Judith, so to speak

definitions.text: Jude is Judith, so to speak

parts.words: Jude is Judith, so to speak
parts.note: say 'Jude is' with a speech defect turning S into TH and it comes out as Judith

explanation.definitionFit: A speech impediment pronouncing S as TH turns 'Jude is' into 'Judith'.

clue.text: Office of Minister of State for the carriage of oil, perhaps

parts.note: port is the way a rifle is carried, as in port arms

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters may be in another order

explanation.surface: A government post responsible for transporting oil.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister's portfolio is the department or office they hold.

clue.text: In Pelion originally it showed how to exaggerate

indicators.note: originally hints the letters were first in another arrangement

explanation.surface: The giants piling Pelion on Ossa showed how to overdo it.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth giants piled Mount Pelion on Mount Ossa to reach heaven, the image behind 'pile Pelion on Ossa', to overdo something.
explanation.definitionFit: To pile it on is to overstate or lay something on thick.

clue.text: Sister, for example, when filled with love

definitions.text: Sister, for example, when filled with love

indicators.note: being filled with means the O goes inside the word for a religious sister

parts.note: a Sister is a nun
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A nun overflowing with affection.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: 'Sister' is an example of a part of speech, and the wordplay is NUN with O inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Sister is a naming word, an example of that part of speech.

clue.text: The richest man in the world in book or play

definitions.text: The richest man in the world in book or play

parts.words: The richest man in the world in book or play
parts.note: Ian Fleming's villain who hoards bullion is presented as the world's richest man, in the novel and the film

explanation.definitionFit: Fleming's Bond villain is a gold-smuggling tycoon billed as fabulously wealthy.

clue.text: The position of the driver

parts.note: the driver is a golfer's club, and the golfer takes up a set position before swinging

explanation.definitionFit: A golfer's posture and feet placement before a shot is their stance.

clue.text: Damage to boat off Gateshead. in rough sea

indicators.note: a rough sea is churned up, so the letters are tossed into a new order

parts.note: read as Gate's head, the first letter of gate, G

explanation.surface: A vessel wrecked off the Tyneside town of Gateshead in stormy waters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gateshead' is read as Gate's head, a single letter; 'rough' mixes it with the boat and the sea. Gateshead is a town on the River Tyne in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Sabotage is deliberate wrecking or destruction of property.

clue.text: The kind of law Carroll's Alice comprehended

indicators.note: comprehended means contained, so the letters sit inside the words

explanation.surface: The sort of rule Lewis Carroll's heroine understood.
explanation.definitionFit: Salic law barred women from succeeding to the throne in some European monarchies.

clue.text: Continue with 50 per cent benefit

parts.note: to be is to exist, to go on
fifty per cent is a half

explanation.surface: Keep going while getting only half the welfare payment.
explanation.definitionFit: Done on someone's behalf means done for their advantage or in their interest.

clue.text: Mounted parade with soldiers in the Roman courts

indicators.note: in a down clue mounted means raised up, so the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: to air is to parade or show off
TA is the Territorial Army, British reserve soldiers

explanation.surface: A cavalry parade with troops in the ancient Roman courtyards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mounted' reverses AIR + TA, giving AT and RIA.
explanation.definitionFit: An atrium was the central open court of a Roman house.

clue.text: A fair amount to drink, one might say

indicators.note: one might say signals the word is spoken, so a drink sounds the same

parts.note: mead is a drink brewed from honey

explanation.surface: A reasonable quantity to have at the bar, you could say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A fair amount' looks like 'quite a lot'; here it means a fitting share.
explanation.definitionFit: A meed is a deserved portion or reward, an archaic word.

clue.text: Discover impostor's real name

indicators.note: an impostor is a fake, so the letters are a false arrangement

explanation.surface: Unmask a fraudster's true identity.
explanation.definitionFit: To find out a fact is to come to know it.

clue.text: The chosen, it is said, of a German prince

parts.note: the elect are those chosen
oral means spoken

explanation.surface: The people selected, so they say, belonging to a German ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: The Electors were German princes who chose the Holy Roman Emperor; the adjective describes them.
explanation.definitionFit: The Electors of the Holy Roman Empire were German princes, and this adjective relates to them.

clue.text: Firm gathered together

explanation.definitionFit: A calm, self-possessed person is steady, and things assembled into one place have been amassed.

clue.text: Printers with a Greek girl? No, she's from New Zealand

parts.note: the NGA was the National Graphical Association, the British printers' union
Io was a maiden of Greek myth loved by Zeus

explanation.surface: Is the printer's companion a Greek lass? No, a Kiwi.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to Ngaio Marsh, the New Zealand crime novelist; it is also a Maori first name.
explanation.definitionFit: A Maori girl's name, borne by the crime writer Ngaio Marsh of Christchurch.
